objective: Choose interventions by the problem outcome and evidence rather than by the capabilities already owned.

problem_contract.statement: Improve the named outcome within explicit constraints, even when the familiar tool does not fit.
problem_contract.framing_policy: Establish the stakeholder outcome and constraints during framing. The initial tool-shaped wording may be corrected; after agreement, preserve the outcome and constraints across competing solutions.

design_budget.execution: Initial catalog design and structural validation; subsequent execution has its own fixed contract under latest_execution.
design_budget.scope: Three rounds for the complete catalog design, not three rounds multiplied by each step.

strategies.title: Rewrite the need before naming tools
strategies.mechanism: Remove the familiar tool from the problem statement before choosing an intervention.
strategies.use_when: The request already specifies a tool but the desired outcome is unclear.
strategies.output: problem brief with success measure and exclusion conditions
strategies.lane_z: Build the strongest case for the requested hammer; attack a case where using it increases output without improving the outcome.
strategies.lane_a: Describe an intervention against the outcome with no dependency on the requested tool.
strategies.example: A growing review queue becomes “reduce waiting time to a useful decision,” rather than “generate more review summaries.”
strategies.falsification: If the brief only makes sense when the incumbent tool is named, reframing has failed.
strategies.failure_mode: Tool terminology sneaks back in as a purported requirement.
strategies.frame_expiry: A stakeholder changes the desired outcome or constraint.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.
strategies.evidence_status: Source-backed artifact analysis and explicitly scoped synthetic/model exercises; no production effectiveness established.
strategies.counterexample_provenance: Actual runs must cite an observed or supplied concrete case. Hypothetical examples are proposed test scenarios, not real counterexample evidence.
strategies.premortem_guardrail: Reject alternatives sharing the incumbent mechanism; retain the original outcome and constraints, and record unresolved evidence with an owner.

strategies.title: Build the hammer and its genuine opposite
strategies.mechanism: Apply the exact two-lane dialectic to an incumbent proposal and a different mechanism.
strategies.use_when: A favored idea is already attracting commitment.
strategies.unit: One adjudicated pair of opposed proposals
strategies.output: claim-by-claim bridge decisions and owned residue
strategies.lane_z: Build the incumbent through generation and critique; include a concrete counterexample.
strategies.lane_a: Hold the problem fixed; propose a solution that changes the intervention mechanism, not its configuration.
strategies.example: Lane Z improves automated reviews; Lane A changes who can decide and removes an unnecessary approval step.
strategies.falsification: Reject the pair if both proposals require the same central mechanism or if one solves a different problem.
strategies.failure_mode: A friendly critic merely helps the incumbent become more polished.
strategies.frame_expiry: The incumbent assumption or shared problem changes.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Investigate the layers before choosing a remedy
strategies.mechanism: Use independent concern-based investigators to discover incompatible explanations.
strategies.use_when: Symptoms span product outcomes, implementation behavior, and operating practice.
inputs: evidence from at least two layers
strategies.output: tension ledger distinguishing contradiction, gap, and speculation
strategies.lane_z: Inspect what the incumbent actually does and where its contract breaks.
strategies.lane_a: Inspect a competing explanation such as approval ownership, missing information, or incentives.
strategies.example: The interface suggests reviews are instant, execution creates summaries quickly, and operators still wait days for an owner decision.
strategies.falsification: A proposed tension fails if the claims concern different times, scopes, or meanings, or lack evidence.
strategies.failure_mode: Several agents repeat the same documentation and mistake agreement for evidence.
strategies.frame_expiry: A changed layer removes the cited contradiction.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Reverse the order: distill, then challenge, then repair
strategies.mechanism: Expose the bias introduced by compression itself before adopting the reduced problem.
strategies.use_when: The original problem is too broad, but shrinking it may hide the essential obstacle.
strategies.unit: One smallest coherent unit with a loss ledger
strategies.output: repaired unit and explicit recomposition contract
strategies.lane_z: Distill the incumbent to its smallest unit and show how it fits the whole.
strategies.lane_a: Challenge the omitted responsibilities and offer a different unit if the reduction preserved the wrong thing.
strategies.example: “Summarize one review” looks coherent until robot-talks shows that the missing responsibility is assigning a decision owner.
strategies.falsification: The unit fails if reconnecting it requires an unnamed coordinator or discards an outcome constraint.
strategies.failure_mode: A neat small unit replaces the actual problem with an easier one.
strategies.frame_expiry: New surrounding workflow or integration obligations appear.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Run an intervention-family tournament
strategies.mechanism: Keep different kinds of intervention alive until comparative evidence eliminates them.
strategies.use_when: There are several plausible solutions and premature commitment is costly.
strategies.unit: One comparable set of three intervention families
strategies.output: viable option set, elimination reasons, and next evidence
strategies.lane_z: Include the strongest incumbent technical proposal.
strategies.lane_a: Include process or ownership change and task removal; alternatives must have different mechanisms.
strategies.example: Compare automation, delegated decision authority, and removing low-value reviews on the same sample of requests.
strategies.falsification: Eliminate proposals that fail a shared constraint; preserve ties when the available evidence cannot discriminate.
strategies.failure_mode: Confidence, novelty, or invented numeric scores choose the winner.
strategies.frame_expiry: A constraint changes or elimination evidence arrives.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Solve a tiny case with the hammer unavailable
strategies.mechanism: Remove the incumbent from a controlled scenario to reveal dependence on tool vocabulary.
strategies.use_when: People cannot imagine solving the problem without the familiar capability.
strategies.unit: One representative toy case with a no-hammer baseline
strategies.lane_z: Run the incumbent on the same small case as a comparison.
strategies.lane_a: Solve the case through a manual, process, or removal intervention without the hammer.
strategies.example: Manually route five requests to empowered reviewers and compare waiting time with an automated-summary baseline.
strategies.falsification: The result fails to transfer if the toy case excludes the real bottleneck, uncertainty, or constraint.
strategies.failure_mode: The artificial case is made so easy that any alternative succeeds.
strategies.frame_expiry: Volume, risk, or case diversity exceeds the toy-case envelope.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Test the causal fork
strategies.mechanism: Design an observation that discriminates between the incumbent diagnosis and a competing cause.
strategies.use_when: A proposed tool addresses a symptom, but the causal explanation is uncertain.
strategies.output: observation with support limits and unresolved confounders
strategies.lane_z: State what should change if the hammer addresses the real cause.
strategies.lane_a: State what should change if a different cause and intervention explain the symptom.
strategies.example: One hypothesis says reviews need clearer summaries; another says only one overloaded person can approve. Test predicted waiting-time changes separately.
strategies.falsification: If both hypotheses predict the same observation, redesign the test; an inconclusive result is not a win.
strategies.failure_mode: A tool success metric is substituted for the problem outcome, or a confounder decides the result.
strategies.frame_expiry: A new confounder or cause invalidates the comparison.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Attack failure residue rather than the happy path
strategies.mechanism: Compare what survives disruption and what damage remains after a mistaken choice.
strategies.use_when: The wrong tool fit could create recurring obligations or costly reversal.
strategies.output: degradation boundary, rollback obligation, and decision residue
strategies.lane_z: Stress the incumbent under missing inputs, overload, or unavailable operators.
strategies.lane_a: Propose a structurally different intervention whose acceptable residue is better under the same stressor.
strategies.example: Automated review summaries continue during overload but accumulate unowned decisions; an ownership rule may preserve a usable decision path.
strategies.falsification: Reject a design when the required outcome cannot survive the named stressor or recovery depends on an unowned action.
strategies.failure_mode: Imaginary disasters justify elaborate protection with no relevant failure evidence.
strategies.frame_expiry: A new realistic stressor or required surviving outcome appears.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Borrow a mechanism through an explicit bridge
strategies.mechanism: Use an outside analogy to generate alternatives, then separate shared causal structure from resemblance.
strategies.use_when: Everyone searches only within the incumbent tool family.
strategies.output: bridge verdict per claim and transfer conditions
strategies.lane_z: Build the incumbent and identify a case where its fit boundary breaks.
strategies.lane_a: Borrow a different mechanism from scheduling, queues, delegation, or removal and test its actual fit.
strategies.example: A queue suggests limiting concurrent work and clarifying service ownership; the analogy alone does not prove either fixes this review process.
strategies.falsification: Reject transfer if the target lacks the mechanism assumed by the analogy; label resemblance-only claims analogy-only.
strategies.failure_mode: An attractive metaphor is treated as implementation evidence.
strategies.frame_expiry: Target-domain differences invalidate the stated transfer condition.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Compare the human need with the machine representation
strategies.mechanism: Detect when a schema can represent only hammer-shaped needs and silently drops the rest.
strategies.use_when: Requests become structured artifacts whose fields favor an existing capability.
strategies.unit: One synchronized human/structured problem record with a loss check
strategies.output: paired records and an owned mismatch ledger
strategies.example: Human text says “waiting for an accountable decision”; the machine form records “summary quality” but has nowhere to record decision ownership.
strategies.falsification: The pair fails when outcome, constraints, exclusions, or unresolved claims differ between the human and machine lanes.
strategies.failure_mode: Two formats duplicate the same bias; synchronization is mistaken for correctness.
strategies.frame_expiry: A new consumer, field, or meaning changes the representation contract.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.human_lane: Preserve the user outcome, constraints, exclusions, evidence, and unresolved claims in prose for human judgment.
strategies.machine_lane: Represent the same meanings in structured fields for agents and validation; expose fields that cannot carry a human obligation.

strategies.title: Compare construction value with operating burden
strategies.mechanism: Give lifecycle cost and human obligations a separate voice in selection.
strategies.use_when: Builders value capability gains while operators inherit the costs.
strategies.output: non-dominated option set and owned support residue
strategies.lane_z: Build the strongest incumbent case, including maintenance and incident obligations.
strategies.lane_a: Offer an intervention with a different recurring burden such as a changed decision rule.
strategies.example: A review agent saves drafting time but requires continual rule tuning; clearer approval rights may solve the same delay with less recurring work.
strategies.falsification: Remove a dominated option only when another is at least as good on every declared relevant dimension and better on one; retain incomparable options.
strategies.failure_mode: Support work becomes an undifferentiated queue that blocks independent prototype work.
strategies.frame_expiry: Operating volume, owner capacity, or burden priorities change.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.title: Make removal, reuse, and delegation selectable exits
strategies.mechanism: Question the need to produce a solution before improving its implementation.
strategies.use_when: Every intake request turns into a construction project.
strategies.unit: One decision menu with a credible non-build exit
strategies.output: bounded route choice with rejection conditions
strategies.lane_z: Build the best version of the requested capability and include full obligation costs.
strategies.lane_a: Consider removing the task, reusing an existing process, delegating the outcome, or bounded observation.
strategies.example: If low-risk requests do not need a review, removing that step may reduce delay more directly than building a faster review tool.
strategies.falsification: An exit is invalid if it sacrifices a required outcome; inaction must include its expected harm and observation period.
strategies.failure_mode: “Do nothing” evades an unmet need or “buy” assumes access that has not been checked.
strategies.frame_expiry: Available alternatives, required outcomes, or inaction costs change.

strategies.title: Alternate building and reframing with a hard budget
strategies.mechanism: Prevent sunk effort from locking the team into its first framing.
strategies.use_when: The team learns during design but repeatedly defaults to polishing the same solution.
strategies.output: revised choice or stable disagreement with next evidence
strategies.lane_z: Generate an incumbent version, attack a concrete counterexample, and revise.
strategies.lane_a: At each checkpoint propose a different mechanism for the unchanged problem.
strategies.example: After each review-agent improvement, test whether ownership change or task removal now better fits the same waiting-time goal.
strategies.falsification: Stop after three rounds or when a round adds only terminology; preserve disagreement if no new evidence resolves it.
strategies.failure_mode: Endless critique consumes delivery time and keeps every option alive.
strategies.frame_expiry: New evidence changes the problem or warrants a new bounded investigation.

strategies.title: Give the method itself an applicability and expiry test
strategies.mechanism: Prevent robot-talks, distill, or governance from becoming the next hammer.
strategies.use_when: A rich workflow is being applied by default to every task.
strategies.output: cheapest adequate route and trigger for escalation
strategies.lane_z: Build the case for using the full investigative workflow and attack its cost on a simple task.
strategies.lane_a: Use direct inspection or one discriminating question when that can resolve the uncertainty.
strategies.example: A clearly bounded label correction needs a direct edit; contradictory review policies across several layers may justify robot-talks.
strategies.falsification: Choose a larger method only for a named unresolved risk or contradiction the smaller method cannot handle.
strategies.failure_mode: The anti-bias framework becomes mandatory ceremony, or cost minimization skips a real contradiction.
strategies.frame_expiry: The task gains cross-layer contradictions or the chosen route fails its stated coverage.
strategies.recomposition: The decision owner consumes this output alongside the unchanged problem brief, constraints, evidence limits, and residue to choose a next intervention.

strategies.direct_exit: If direct inspection or a clearly bounded action adequately resolves the task, stop with that route choice; skip both proposed skill stages. Escalate only on a named unresolved contradiction or coverage failure.

strategies.title: Invert the assumption to open another mechanism
strategies.mechanism: Reverse a presumed necessity, role relation, or causal direction and turn the reversal into a testable alternative.
strategies.use_when: The analysis assumes the current intervention is necessary or that causality runs in only one direction.
strategies.unit: One typed inversion with an alternative mechanism and discriminating test
strategies.output: inversion ledger with candidate mechanism, discriminating test, and evidence limits
strategies.lane_z: Build the incumbent claim and attack its applicability with a sourced concrete counterexample.
strategies.lane_a: Explore the reversed assumption and propose a genuinely different feasible intervention for the same outcome.
strategies.example: “More review automation reduces delay” becomes “When could fewer mandatory reviews reduce delay while preserving required assurance?” This opens risk-based exemptions as a candidate rather than assuming the inverse is true.
strategies.falsification: Reject an inversion that changes the required outcome, violates a constraint, implies an unsupported logical equivalence, or yields only a renamed incumbent.
strategies.failure_mode: Negating an assertion is mistaken for disproving it, or an appealing reversal is treated as causal evidence.
strategies.frame_expiry: New evidence changes the original premise, inference validity, or feasible alternative.

strategies.title: Attack with the goal of expanding the design space
strategies.mechanism: Translate a specific critique into a new degree of freedom, different candidate mechanisms, and a feasible discriminating test.
strategies.use_when: Critique only rejects proposals or repairs the incumbent without opening genuinely different possibilities.
strategies.unit: One attack-to-opening record with candidate mechanisms and next evidence
strategies.output: expansion ledger linking attacks, assumptions, openings, candidate mechanisms, dispositions, and tests
strategies.lane_z: Build the incumbent and attack a specific dependency, boundary, or failure behavior with evidence.
strategies.lane_a: Use the exposed assumption to propose a different mechanism; the creative translator supports expansion without replacing the independent Lane A owner.
strategies.example: “Automated summaries leave decisions unowned” opens delegated decision rights, explicit escalation rules, or removing unnecessary approval steps; each candidate still needs outcome evidence.
strategies.falsification: Reject unsupported attack conclusions and candidates disconnected from the exposed assumption or shared outcome. A hard constraint or no feasible opening is a legitimate terminal disposition.
strategies.failure_mode: Destruction becomes performance, every objection forces invented alternatives, or novelty and option count replace fit.
strategies.frame_expiry: The critique is disproved, the exposed assumption changes, or new evidence closes an apparent opening.

analysis_lenses.logical_inversion: Invert a presumed necessity, causal direction, or role relation to generate testable different mechanisms while preserving the outcome. Exploratory reversal is not logical equivalence.
analysis_lenses.attack_to_expand: Convert a critique into an exposed assumption, new degree of freedom, candidate mechanism, and discriminating test; preserve hard constraints and infeasible openings honestly.
analysis_lenses.status: local-design-extension; requested by user; not empirically tested
